did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezra chapter 2 describes the exiles’ return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah, with each person returning to his own city.
Did you know? Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and other leaders are listed at the head of those who returned, and the chapter refers to them all together as “the people of Israel.”
Did you know? The chapter includes a detailed list of families and ancestral houses, with the number of people who came from each one.
Did you know? The priests are also listed among the families of the people, including the descendants of Jedaiah, Immer, Pashhur, and Harim.
Did you know? The number of Levites mentioned in the list was much smaller than the number of priests: seventy-four Levites.
Did you know? The chapter also mentions the singers, including 128 members of the family of Asaph.
Did you know? The gatekeepers are listed as a separate group, including the families of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai.
Did you know? At the end of the list of the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants, their total number is given as 392.
Did you know? Some of those who returned could not prove their ancestry or show that their families belonged to their ancestral houses, so it was unclear whether they were Israelites.

Did you know? Priestly families who could not produce their genealogical records were excluded from the priesthood, and they were told not to eat the most holy food until a priest could be identified who had the Urim and Thummim.
Did you know? The entire assembly numbered 42,360 people, not including the male and female servants and the singers, who were counted separately.

Did you know? The heads of the ancestral houses donated from their own possessions to the treasury for the work on the house of God; later in the chapter, gifts of gold, silver, and priestly garments are mentioned.
Did you know? The chapter ends with those who returned settling in their cities: the priests, Levites, people, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, and all Israel.
